title: Immunization Services Decision Table — Combining the Scheduling Allowances for a Series Dose
content:
Pharmacy Clinical Services decision table, Immunization Services. It fixes how Kestrel's scheduling allowances for a phone appointment for the next dose of a vaccination series — the missed-visit allowance, the plan-check allowance, the resumed-series allowance and the outside-record allowance — combine into one combined allowance in days.

**Rule.** The allowances combine in one of three ways. Where the course the series history is on is closed and holds at least one dose entry, the four allowances are added together. Where that course is open and holds at least one dose entry, only the largest of the four applies. Where it holds no dose entry, no allowance applies.

**Conditions read.** "Closed" means the course carries a closing date (it was completed or cancelled); "open" means it carries none. A dose entry is a dose-given entry on the course, whoever gave the dose.

| Course carries a closing date | Dose entries on the course | Combined allowance |
|---|---|---|
| yes | one or more | the four allowances added together |
| no | one or more | the largest of the four allowances |
| yes | none | none |
| no | none | none |

**Hypothetical illustrations.** Suppose the four allowances come to 2 days, nothing, 1 day and 3 days.

- Closed course with two dose entries: 2 plus 0 plus 1 plus 3, a combined allowance of 6 days.
- Open course with two dose entries: the largest of the four, 3 days.
- Course with no dose entry: no allowance, 0 days, whatever the four come to.
- Open course with one dose entry where all four allowances are nothing: the largest is nothing, 0 days.
